correctness.rationale: The included deterministic code recursively enumerates all 3n/2-edge perfect matchings, and generates precisely all faces from their subsets. The staged codimension-one toggle matching is checked for disjointness; all 1,161,740 faces and 7,902,995 covering incidences across eight graph complexes are traversed in the fully oriented reversed-match Hasse diagrams, with acyclic topological sorts. For open/periodic n=2,4,6,8, the unmatched nonempty cells have ranks (0,1 in degree 1,1 in degree 2,2 in degree 3) and (0,3 in degree 1,3 in degree 2,12 in degree 3). The empty face is matched in each instance. Breaking its pair produces one ordinary critical vertex, with all other critical cells in one dimension; Forman Morse theory gives exactly the stated wedges/points. The standalone checker was actually run and generated the embedded output. Its finite scope is explicit; no infinite induction is claimed.

value.rationale: The first verified natural cutoff where transverse boundary closure changes the amplification of perfect-matching-complex sphere multiplicity (one versus three at width four, one versus three at width six, two versus twelve at width eight) is a mathematically motivated finite case, not an arbitrary slice. It settles the previously conjectural rectangular 3-by-8 instance and determines exact sphere dimensions as well as homology, while the triangle-periodic comparison isolates a boundary effect not implied by known two-row results. These benchmarks can guide future universal boundary-recurrence methods; no such future theorem is claimed.
